points.description: Chooses state x1 = θ, x2 = θ̇ (equivalent choice acceptable) and writes both state equations: ẋ1 = x2 and ẋ2 = (1/J)(τ − b x2 − mgℓ sin x1). Both equations must be correct for full marks.

levels.says: State vector chosen and one of the two equations correct, or both equations present with a minor algebra/sign slip.

points.description: Equilibrium condition: x2 = 0 and mgℓ sin θe = τ0, together with the existence range |τ0| ≤ mgℓ = 2.4525 N·m (g = 9.81), because |sin θe| ≤ 1. A range with no equilibrium equation, or an equilibrium equation with no range, earns no credit for the range.

levels.says: Correct equilibrium equation and range given symbolically as |τ0| ≤ mgℓ without evaluating the number.
Correct equilibrium equation and numerical range written as τ0 ≤ 2.4525 N·m without the modulus, with symmetry (negative torque) not mentioned anywhere.

rubric.notes: Full marks: correct two-equation state model, and equilibrium equation with the evaluated range |τ0| ≤ 2.4525 N·m. Half of the second mark for the symbolic range, or for the one-sided range with no mention of symmetry. Equilibrium equation without any range earns 0 for the second point. Claiming a unique equilibrium is not penalised in the marks, but note it.
rubric.answer_key: x1 = θ, x2 = θ̇. ẋ1 = x2; ẋ2 = (1/J)(τ − b x2 − mgℓ sin x1). With τ = τ0 and ẋ = 0: x2 = 0 and mgℓ sin θe = τ0, with mgℓ = 1×9.81×0.25 = 2.4525 N·m. Since |sin θe| ≤ 1, an equilibrium exists only when |τ0| ≤ 2.4525 N·m (two equilibria in each period for |τ0| < 2.4525).
